text.text: Everything the development team runs on: donors and their giving, gifts and pledges, campaigns against goal and the thank-you calls that keep people giving. Start with the Dashboard each Monday, then work the Overdue and Mine views. Record every gift the day it arrives, and mark the thank-you done the same week.

How to read the numbers

cells.text: Total received from that donor: under 500 is Annual, 500 and over is Mid-level, 5,000 and over is Major
Assign a named owner to every Major donor; review Mid-level donors twice a year
Gifts received for the campaign divided by its goal; pledges are not counted until received
Under 50 percent with half the time gone means adding an ask or a second push
Pledges still open for that donor
Call before the due date, not after it

text.text: A gift is not finished until it is recorded, receipted and thanked. This routine keeps all three inside one week.
The same day a gift arrives
Open the Gifts table and add a row. Name it with the campaign and donor, and fill in amount, method and date.
Link the gift to the donor and the campaign it counts toward. If the donor is new, add them first from the intake form.
Set Status to Received. A pledge stays Pledged until the money is actually in hand.
Deposit checks within two working days and note any restriction the donor wrote on the check or card.
Within a week
Send the tax receipt. Use the standard receipt wording your accountant approved.
Make the thank-you call or write the letter, then press Mark thanked on the gift.
Add a follow-up for the donor if they asked a question or mentioned a program they love.
Common mistakes
Counting a pledge as received: the campaign total will look better than the bank balance.
Recording one gift against two campaigns: split it into two rows with the right amounts.
Forgetting matching gifts: ask every business donor whether their employer matches.
Donors rarely leave because of a mistake. They leave because nobody told them what their gift did. Stewardship is the plan that prevents that.
What every donor should hear
A personal thank-you within 48 hours of any gift.
An honest update on the program their gift supports, at least twice a year.
An invitation to see the work in person, once a year.
By giving level

cells.text: Visit or call each quarter, plus a personal note after every gift
Call after each gift, update email every two months, one invitation a year
Letter after each gift, newsletter and one appeal a quarter

text.text: When a donor goes quiet
Check the donor row. If Lapsed, look at the last gift date and the last follow-up.
Make one warm call that asks nothing. Ask what they thought of the last update.
If they want to stop, set the stage to Declined and note why.
If they come back, set Active and thank them like a new donor.
Every campaign gets a row, a goal and a lead before the first message goes out. A goal nobody wrote down cannot be missed or met.
Before launch
Create the campaign row. Write the purpose in one sentence a donor would repeat.
Set a goal from last year's result plus a realistic stretch, not a wish.
Name a lead and list every follow-up in the Follow-ups table with a due date.
Build the thank-you plan first. Who calls whom, and when.
During the campaign
Check Goal reached (%) every Monday.
Move the campaign to Live only when the first message is ready to send.
Chase pledges due this week before asking for anything new.
After it closes
Press Close campaign once the last gift is recorded.
Count thank-yous done against gifts received. Anything missing goes on this week's list.
Write three lines on what worked and what to change, in the campaign row's page.
